declaration.preface: Alchem International Pvt. Ltd. is committed to maintaining the highest standards of labour and human rights across all its operations. As a global leader in the production of plant-derived active pharmaceutical ingredients, fine chemicals, and herbal extracts, Alchem recognizes that the well-being, dignity, and safety of its employees are central to the company’s success and sustainability. This Labour & Humanx Rights Policy reflects our commitment to fostering a fair, inclusive, and respectful workplace where every individual is valued and treated with integrity. Through this policy, Alchem seeks to ensure compliance with all applicable laws, uphold internationally recognized human rights principles, and promote a culture of equity, safety, and continuous development for all members of our workforce.
declaration.declaration: Alchem International Pvt. Ltd. is committed to upholding and promoting the highest standards of labour and human rights across all aspects of its business operations. Our practices are guided by ethical responsibility, legal compliance, and respect for every individual who contributes to our success.
declaration.scope: This policy is applicable across all employees, workers, contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, and business partners of Alchem International Pvt. Ltd.. It also extends to the communities in which we operate, ensuring that our commitment to upholding labour rights, human dignity, and ethical workplace practices is embedded throughout our global value chain. By including our suppliers and other stakeholders, we aim to promote fair labour practices, respect for human rights, and decent working conditions beyond our own operations, driving positive social impact across the industry. This Policy is only applicable to the below-mentioned location:

focusAreas: Child Labour, Forced Labour and Human Trafficking
External Stakeholder Human Rights & Supply Chain

Employees Health and Safety: Alchem maintains robust health and safety management systems designed to protect every member of our workforce. Regular risk assessments, safety trainings, provision of appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), and periodic medical check-ups are integral to our operations. Our manufacturing facility complies with national and international safety regulations, and potential workplace hazards are continually identified, assessed, and mitigated.
Regular HSE audits are conducted across all facilities to identify risks and implement corrective measures, ensuring a safe and compliant workplace.
Periodic risk assessments help identify potential hazards and establish proactive measures to prevent workplace incidents.
Working Hours and Overtime Policy: We ensure fair wages, transparent benefits, and reasonable working hours in full compliance with applicable labour laws and international standards. Alchem promotes open communication between management and employees to ensure that all work-related concerns are heard, addressed, and resolved promptly. Health and wellness initiatives, including periodic health examinations, reinforce our commitment to employee well-being.
Two-way communication systems, including suggestion boxes and digital portals, enable employees to share feedback and raise workplace concerns transparently.
Labour Relations: Alchem respects the rights of employees to freely associate, join representative bodies, and engage in collective bargaining, in accordance with applicable laws. We encourage open dialogue and collaboration between management and employees to maintain mutual trust, fairness, and continuous improvement in workplace relations.
Career Management: We invest in the professional growth of our employees through structured learning, skill enhancement, and leadership development programs. Alchem is dedicated to creating an environment where every individual has equal access to opportunities for advancement, continuous learning, and personal growth.
Continuous training on safety, leadership, and technical skills empowers employees and supports their professional growth.
Child Labour, Forced Labour and Human Tr: Alchem enforces a strict zero-tolerance policy against child labour, forced labour, and human trafficking within its operations and supply chain. We actively conduct supplier due diligence and audits to ensure that our ethical standards are upheld throughout our value chain. We remain vigilant in identifying, preventing, and addressing any risks related to human rights violations.
Equal Opportunity and Non-Discrimination: Alchem is committed to a workplace that is free from discrimination and harassment of any kind. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, qualifications, and performance—without regard to gender, age, race, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or other protected characteristics. We celebrate diversity as a strength and cultivate an inclusive culture that empowers all individuals to achieve their fullest potential.
External Stakeholder Human Rights: Alchem respects and upholds the human rights of local communities, customers, suppliers, and business partners. We engage proactively with stakeholders to ensure that our operations contribute positively to society, safeguard community well-being, and avoid any adverse human rights impacts.
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI): Workshops and awareness sessions promote diversity, equality, and a culture of mutual respect within the organization.
Harassment and Discrimination: Alchem is committed to a workplace that is free from discrimination and harassment of any kind.
Alchem engages with communities, clients, and partners to promote collective responsibility and collaboration in advancing human rights and ethical practices.

targets.target: Achieve 0% workplace incident rate by FY 2027–28 through enhanced safety training, regular risk assessments, and proactive hazard mitigation.
Maintain 100% compliance with all applicable local, national, and international health and safety regulations across manufacturing site.
Conduct annual medical check-ups for 100% of employees and contractors.
Ensure provision of certified PPE to all relevant staff and conduct periodic fire safety, EHS, and emergency preparedness training sessions.
Conduct quarterly internal EHS audits and annual third-party audits to validate compliance and continual improvement.
targets.deadline: Quarterly internal audits; annual third-party audits

targets.target: Ensure 100% of employees have access to open, two-way communication channels such as digital feedback portals, suggestion boxes, or grievance platforms by FY 2027–28.
Maintain working hours within 8 hours/day and 48 hours/week, ensuring at least one weekly day off, with overtime being voluntary and within legal limits.
Provide overtime pay at double the basic wage, with annual reviews of wages and benefits to ensure competitiveness and fairness.
Conduct semi-annual employee engagement surveys to assess workplace satisfaction and well-being.
Maintain 0 working condition incident by FY 2027–28 through enhanced safety training, regular risk assessments, and proactive hazard mitigation.
Increase employee participation in collective dialogue and engagement forums by 15% by FY 2027–28.
Conduct quarterly meetings with employee representatives to review workplace conditions and address concerns.
Maintain 100% freedom of association and collective bargaining rights for all eligible employees in compliance with national labour laws.
Provide training and development opportunities to 100% of employees by FY 2027–28.
Organize a minimum of one upskilling or technical training workshop per quarter for plant, R&D, and corporate employees.
Deliver a minimum of 10 hours of human rights and ethics training annually to all employees by FY 2027–28.
Implement succession and leadership programs across departments to strengthen internal talent pipelines.

quantitative.area: Child Labour, Forced Labour & Human Trafficking

targets.target: Maintain 100% compliance with national and international standards prohibiting child labour, forced labour, and human trafficking by FY 2027–28.
Ensure 100% of employees and suppliers receive awareness training on labour standards and human trafficking prevention.
Maintain zero incidents of child labour, forced labour, or human trafficking across operations and supply chain.
Verify that no workers under the age of 18 are employed and that all Tier 1 suppliers comply with Alchem’s labour standards.
Achieve 15% women representation in the overall workforce and 25% representation of women on the Board or senior leadership by FY 2027–28.
Reach gender parity in managerial and leadership roles by FY 2027–28.
Increase workforce representation from underrepresented communities by 10% by FY 2027–28.
Conduct annual DEI workshops and sensitivity training for all employees.
Monitor progress through a dedicated DEI Committee, publishing annual diversity performance metrics.
Maintain zero tolerance and zero incident of workplace harassment or discrimination by FY 2027–28.
Deliver annual anti-harassment and anti-discrimination training to 100% of employees.
Maintain a confidential grievance redressal mechanism, accessible 24x7 via digital and offline channels.
Ensure 100% of complaints are addressed within 14 working days, with documented resolution and follow-up actions.
Conduct anonymous workplace culture and inclusivity surveys annually to evaluate progress.
Maintain a 24x7 anonymous grievance reporting system, supported by structured escalation through HR and Compliance Committees.
Conduct biannual reviews of grievance cases and outcomes to ensure timely closure, transparency, and employee confidence.
Ensure zero retaliation against employees who raise concerns in good faith.

quantitative.area: External Stakeholder Human Rights & Supply Chain

targets.target: Conduct human rights impact assessments for 100% of Tier 1 suppliers and at least 75% of Tier 2 suppliers annually.
Integrate human rights and labour standards clauses into all supplier contracts and procurement procedures.
Participate in at least one multi-stakeholder or industry-led human rights initiative per year to promote collective responsibility and best practices in ethical sourcing.
Develop supplier capacity-building programs to enhance compliance with Alchem’s Code of Conduct and sustainability standards.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees the implementation of Alchem’s Labour & Human Rights Policy, ensures compliance with all applicable labour laws, and addresses employee relations and workplace well-being concerns.
Monitors safety standards and environmental practices across all facilities, ensuring a secure, healthy, and compliant work environment for all employees.
Drives initiatives to achieve Alchem’s diversity, equity, and inclusion objectives, promoting a respectful and inclusive workplace culture.
All leaders and employees share responsibility for upholding labour and human rights principles, maintaining ethical conduct, and contributing to a safe and fair workplace.

policy.monitoring:
Employee Feedback Surveys: Alchem conducts regular employee feedback surveys to evaluate satisfaction with workplace conditions, health and safety standards, and career growth opportunities, ensuring continuous improvement in employee well-being and engagement.

Internal assessments and third-party audits, such as sustainability and compliance evaluations, are conducted to verify adherence to established KPIs and standards.

Alchem regularly aligns its practices with evolving global labour and human rights standards, including the UN SDGs, ILO conventions, and industry best practices.

Employee and stakeholder feedback is actively collected and analyzed to identify improvement areas and enhance workplace policies.
policy.reviewMechanism:
Alchem International Pvt. Ltd. is committed to maintaining the accuracy, transparency, and effectiveness of its Labour & Human Rights Policy through continuous evaluation and enhancement.

The policy and related practices will be reviewed annually by a cross-functional team with inputs from employees, management, and external stakeholders to ensure ongoing relevance.

The Labour & Human Rights Policy will be reviewed annually by the Human Resources Director for its effectiveness, and relevance. This review will ensure that the policy adapts to changing regulations, stakeholder feedback, and evolving company goals. Updates and changes will be communicated to all employees and stakeholders as necessary.

The company strives to achieve and sustain zero incidents of workplace discrimination, harassment, or safety violations through proactive prevention and accountability.
